newsitem.title: LATVIA: Baltic MPs urge work for quick NATO entry.
newsitem.headline: Baltic MPs urge work for quick NATO entry.

text.p: Baltic members of parliament urged their governments on Sunday to work out joint action for quick entry into NATO despite a warning by U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry that their countries are not ready for membership.
Hopes by Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia for quick NATO entry were dented after Perry said they were not yet ready to join the alliance as they could not come to the defence of other member states.
Meeting at the Baltic Assembly, which groups Baltic deputies and makes non-binding resolutions and recommendations to governments, MPs said efforts to enter NATO soon press ahead.

"The Baltic Assembly appeals to the governments of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania without delay to develop a common policy and take effective joint preparatory steps...to facilitate an early accession to NATO by all three Baltic states," the assembly said in a resolution adopted at the meeting.

The Baltic states, which regained independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991, want NATO membership as they remain wary of Russia, which ruled them for most of the last two centuries and which many Balts still see as a potential threat.
The Balts are members of Partnership for Peace (PfP), a programme of cooperation and technical help but without security guarantees, and have troops in the NATO-led force in Bosnia.
NATO has indicated it is likely to begin the process of taking in some new mmbers -- possibly Poland, Hungary and the Czech republic -- next year, but has so far held the Balts at arms length.

Moscow is against NATO expansion as a whole but is very sensitive about the Baltic states, which share thousands of kilometres (miles) of border with Russia and where hundreds of thousands of ethnic Russians still live.
